description: I like to play games and developing them.
summary:
🚀 Mission Nova is a browser game that makes you the mission designer. Over 10 planning decisions, like choosing your rocket, you balance Budget, Room, Power, Comms, Time, Fuel, Food and Science. A live dashboard shows how your spacecraft is doing, surprise events test your design, and a Moon-landing mini-game puts your skills to the test.

🌍 How it addresses the Space Mission Design Game challenge: It turns real mission design into play. Every choice has trade-offs, so players learn that a good mission is a balanced one. At the end, a readiness score from CML 1 to 4, inspired by NASA/JPL's Concept Maturity Levels, shows how mature their design is. Each answer comes with a short science explanation and links to NASA learning pages.

⭐ Why it matters: Missions succeed through careful planning, not just powerful rockets. Mission Nova brings that idea to students and families in any browser, with no installation, and up to 4 players can compare their designs on the same question.
details:
What it does and how it works

🚀 Mission Nova lets you be the mission planner, not just the pilot. Before anything launches, you make 10 big decisions, like which rocket to build, and each one has 3 options. Every choice costs something and gives something back, so you have to balance Budget, Room, Power, Comms, Time, Fuel, Food and Science.

📊 A live dashboard shows how your spacecraft is doing as the plan comes together. After each choice, a short explanation tells you the real science behind it, with a link to NASA learning pages if you want to know more.

⚠️ Surprise events test your plan, and a Moon-landing mini-game puts your skills to the test. At the end, you get a mission readiness score from 1 to 4, inspired by NASA/JPL's Concept Maturity Levels.

👥 Up to 4 players can join. Everyone answers the same question in turn, so you can see how different choices lead to different missions.

Benefits

  • Players see that space missions are about trade-offs: more fuel means less room, and more power means more cost.
  • It needs no installation. It is a single HTML file that runs offline on any modern device.
  • It works for classrooms and families, because several players can share one screen.
  • Keyboard and tap controls, short explanations and a pause menu make it easier to use.

Intended impact

We want players, especially students, to understand how real mission planning works. We want them to learn to weigh limited resources, and we hope the game encourages them to look further at NASA's own educational resources.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

  • Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with no frameworks or libraries.
  • Spacecraft and icon art drawn as SVG in code. The landing mini-game uses the HTML canvas.
  • Images generated with Google Flow, and sounds and voices generated with ElevenLabs.
  • Fredoka font from Google Fonts.
  • Claude by Anthropic, used as an AI assistant for text and code.
  • NASA/JPL Concept Maturity Levels dataset and NASA education pages as the knowledge sources.
  • Hardware: any computer, tablet or phone with a web browser.

How it is creative

The usual space game is about flying, but this one is about planning, and it shows the choices engineers make before launch. Each decision shows its costs on screen, and each answer teaches something through a short explanation. Players take turns on the same question, so the game also becomes a conversation about different strategies. The readiness report uses real NASA vocabulary in a form a student can read.

Factors we considered

  • Accuracy: the numbers are simplified for play, and the game says so. It states that it is independent and not endorsed by NASA.
  • Accessibility: large buttons, number keys and a layout that works on phones.
  • Fairness in multiplayer: every player answers the same question, in turn.
  • Source credit and rights: NASA sources are listed and their licenses noted, and we label AI-generated images and sounds.
  • Reliability: one self-contained file with no network needed.
